nodes.summary: The Cook–Levin theorem and its machinery: SAT verifiers, dense and binary CNF encodings and converters between them, tableau formulas and the generator machines that emit them.
nodes.title: Cook–Levin theorem

nodes.summary: Vertex, edge, list and precoloring-extension coloring, achromatic number, graph homomorphism, maximum and k-cuts, bisection, multiway cut, partition into triangles or paths, bandwidth, linear arrangement and linear ordering.
nodes.title: Graph coloring, cuts and layouts

nodes.summary: Clique, independent set, vertex cover, domination variants, feedback vertex and arc sets, odd cycle transversal, bicliques, densest subgraph, induced matching and minimum fill-in.
nodes.title: Cliques, covers and domination in graphs

nodes.summary: Subset sum, subset product, partition, 3-partition, multiway partition, knapsack variants, bin and strip packing, numerical 3-dimensional matching and 0-1 integer programming.
nodes.title: Number partitioning, knapsack and packing

nodes.summary: Hamiltonian paths and cycles, longest paths and cycles, disjoint paths and path covers, constrained spanning and Steiner trees, minimum equivalent digraph, traveling salesperson and vehicle routing, and (induced) subgraph isomorphism.
nodes.title: Paths, cycles, trees and subgraph problems

nodes.summary: Variants of SAT and CSP: 3SAT and the SAT-to-3SAT reduction, bounded-occurrence, monotone, not-all-equal and 1-in-3 SAT, MAX-SAT, MAX-2SAT, MIN-ONES, circuit SAT, binary CSP and betweenness.
nodes.title: Satisfiability and constraint satisfaction

nodes.summary: Single-machine, parallel-machine, flow-shop, precedence-constrained and resource-constrained scheduling with deadlines, tardiness or weighted completion objectives.
nodes.title: Scheduling problems

nodes.summary: 3-dimensional matching, exact cover, set cover, set packing, set splitting, maximum coverage, minimum test set, generalized and quadratic assignment, facility location, k-center and k-median.
nodes.title: Set systems, assignment and location

nodes.summary: String problems (closest string, longest common subsequence, shortest common supersequence) and puzzles (Sudoku, Nonogram, Akari, Minesweeper, Latin square completion).
nodes.title: Strings, puzzles and Latin squares

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
